name: Light triad vs dark triad

lead: The Dark Triad (Machiavellianism, narcissism, psychopathy) was described by Paulhus and Williams in 2002; the Light Triad (Kantianism, humanism, faith in humanity) was proposed by Scott Barry Kaufman and colleagues in 2019. In looksmaxxing forums the terms are also used for facial and style impressions: warm, trustworthy-looking faces versus cold, intense ones.

Members debate which presentation attracts more, and some adjust grooming, expression and styling accordingly. Psychology research on the personality traits is substantial; research on 'light' or 'dark' facial looks as forum users mean it is not established.

paras: Practically, people discuss softer expressions, warmer eye contact, lighter colouring and approachable styling for a light look, and sharper, harder framing for a dark one. It is talk about presentation rather than a defined protocol.
No physical risk. The Dark Triad literature links its traits to selfish and aggressive outcomes, so adopting the persona rather than the look carries social costs documented in that research.

angle.text: Forum members use the labels to think about which first impression they want to project through expression, grooming and colouring. The idea is that approachable versus intimidating presentation shifts how others react.

lead: The Dark Triad, introduced by Delroy Paulhus and Kevin Williams in 2002, groups three non-clinical traits: Machiavellianism, subclinical narcissism and subclinical psychopathy [1]. The Light Triad was proposed by Scott Barry Kaufman and colleagues as a contrast, consisting of Kantianism (treating people as ends), humanism, and faith in humanity [2].

On looksmax.org the vocabulary has been borrowed for appearance and demeanor: 'light triad looks' for warm, trustworthy faces and 'dark triad looks' for cold, intense ones, with threads arguing which attracts more [3][4].
Research on the personality measures exists; no published study tests the forum usage of 'looks' as defined there.

paras: The Dark Triad traits overlap empirically while remaining conceptually distinct, and low agreeableness is their strongest Big Five correlate [1]. The Light Triad is not simply the inverse: Kaufman's team tested the 12-item Light Triad Scale across four samples (N = 1,518) and reported it predicted life satisfaction and growth-oriented outcomes beyond existing personality measures, whereas the Dark Triad related negatively to these [2].

Dark Triad traits are associated with an accelerated mating strategy, including more partners and favourable attitudes to casual sex [1]. Among the three, narcissism is the one linked to self-rated attractiveness and mate value; facial features associated with dark traits tend to be rated less attractive, and evidence on reproductive success is mixed [1].

Threads titled for light triad looks claim that warm, trustworthy faces win more partners than dark ones; others argue the reverse, and some call the distinction unimportant [3][4]. Participants also describe lighter hair and eye colour as part of a light impression, and 'high trust' appearance as helpful for approachability [4]. These are forum opinions rather than measured findings.
No studies found on 'light triad looks' or 'dark triad looks' as forum users define them. Personality-questionnaire studies of the triads are summarised above [1][2].
